title: Hosting paths & compliance scan with Ridgeway Capitals
next_steps: Send region-specific SOC2/HIPAA evidence pack by 2028-09-13
Schedule 2-hour technical deep dive on networking and KMS for 2028-09-18
Provide quote for 3-month Dedicated pilot with migration assistance
action_items: Marco Alvarez - run latency and cost estimate for Ridgeway's 90M monthly tokens - 2028-09-18
Nina Rao - provide list of EU subsidiaries and legal entities that require residency - 2028-09-14
Ivy Chen - share SOC2 report, HIPAA attestation summary, and Private deployment runbook - 2028-09-13
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-09-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ivy Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Nina Rao (CTO, Ridgeway), Paul Mendes (Head of Compliance), Samir Patel (Infra Ops)
Recording id: ff-20280911-8723

Summary: quick discovery on hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), residency constraints across EU and APAC subsidiaries, logging retention and eDiscovery, KMS residency requirements, and initial pilot next steps.
Topics: hosting models, key management residency, audit logs & legal hold, network connectivity, migration window, timeline and success criteria.

[00:00] Ivy Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I know time is tight so we can run through the high level then Marco will jump into the tech specifics. Nina, Paul, Samir, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Nina Rao: Yeah thanks, appreciate it. Quick note we are rotating our inference traffic off premise but keeping PII and transaction detail in-region, so looking for clarity on residency and what falls into logs.
[00:25] Marco Alvarez: Great, quick question, when you say logs do you mean full request/response transcripts or obfuscated metadata like token counts and latencies?
[00:34] Paul Mendes: Both. For audits we need the request id mapping and timestamps, but we also have to make sure raw customer text doesn't leave EU. So anything that could be PII, we want it redacted or never leave the EU boundary.
[00:48] Samir Patel: And we may need legal hold for a subset of trades for 7 years, so retention windows plus eDiscovery export paths are a must.
[00:57] Ivy Chen: Totally, that's a common ask for asset managers. High level: Redwood Hosted keeps inference in our managed regions, we can pin processing to eu-west and also avoid cross-border backups. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our cloud with tenancy isolation and more SLAs. Private gives you a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem, with local KMS.
[01:20] Nina Rao: Sounds good. A few details: first, residency for keys. We have an internal rule that private keys for decrypting PII must be in the same jurisdiction as the data. Can Redwood support a bring-your-own-key in an EU KMS with no key material leaving region?
[01:35] Marco Alvarez: Yes, with Private we support BYOK where you manage the KMS, or we can integrate with customer-controlled Cloud KMS in a locked region. For Dedicated we offer a customer-specific KMS instance that can be configured with region-only key material and HSM-backed storage. There was a small note though, sometimes the control plane metadata is shared with our control tier, we can limit that.
[01:58] Paul Mendes: That control plane metadata is one of our blockers. We need to know what PII might still be logged by control systems, and whether audit logs for deployments contain payload snippets.
[02:09] Marco Alvarez: Understood. We have an audit path: deployment and infrastructure logs do not include request bodies by default. Access logs are metadata-only, though there are optional debug traces which - and that is sometimes miscaptured by our tooling - may temporarily contain snippets. Those are off by default and require opt-in.
[02:30] Nina Rao: Ok, we will need that documented — the exact fields in each log type.
[02:35] Ivy Chen: We'll share our log schema doc in the follow-up. Link: https://redwood.example.com/security-docs (note: placeholder link shared live).
[02:44] Samir Patel: Network connectivity — we plan to peer our VPCs to a cloud region and allow egress only via a NAT. Is that supported for Dedicated?
[02:55] Marco Alvarez: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints. For Private deployments you manage the networking completely. For Hosted we can limit egress to region but it's through our managed endpoints. We can also support IP allowlists and private link type setups.
[03:14] Paul Mendes: On compliance, we need SOC2 plus a third party HIPAA attestation for our use case. Does Redwood have HIPAA coverage in hosted mode?
[03:24] Ivy Chen: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II. For HIPAA, we have customers on Dedicated and Private configurations that meet HIPAA obligations, especially when you combine private control plane and customer KMS. We do sign BAAs for Dedicated and Private — that's our recommendation for PHI.
[03:40] Nina Rao: Would Hosted be a non-starter then? We have some non-PHI models that could live hosted but anything with PHI or transaction PII needs stronger guarantees.
[03:48] Marco Alvarez: Hosted could be used for non-PII or anonymized workloads. For PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[03:55] Nina Rao: Understood.
[03:58] [04:00] Speaker 3: (overlap) quick question about backups...
[04:03] Ivy Chen: Backups are an important point — we can restrict backups to the same region and disable cross-region snapshots if needed for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted there are region constraints but some infra-level backups may replicate for durability unless we set retention policies.
[04:19] Samir Patel: Do you offer a mode where request payloads are never persisted to disk, only processed in memory? We were thinking streaming-only with ephemeral KV cache flushed on completion.
[04:31] Marco Alvarez: Yes, we have an in-memory processing mode that minimizes persistence; the KV cache is ephemeral and can be disabled. But note this impacts cold-start and may increase cost because caching improves throughput.
[04:48] Paul Mendes: Cost tradeoff noted. Another thing: eDiscovery exports need to be provable chain of custody. We need signed, time-stamped audit events and an export procedure that preserves integrity.
[05:01] Marco Alvarez: We can emit signed audit events and S3 export bundles with checksums. For Private deployments you can run the export into your own bucket so it never crosses jurisdictional boundaries.
[05:14] Nina Rao: Are there any known issues with model fine-tuning or evals that require data to be pooled centrally? We want to run prompt quality checks but cannot send raw corpora to a global telemetry stack.
[05:27] Ivy Chen: Good callout. Redwood Optimize can run locally or in-region for quality monitoring; we also support synthetic evals or hashed telemetry. We would not require raw data to be pooled outside the region for the features you describe.
[05:42] Samir Patel: For the migration plan, we have a legacy inference cluster that holds 12 months of telemetry. We expect to replay a batch migration over a two-week window and then run a pilot of 5% traffic to Redwood Dedicated for 30 days. Any guidance?
[05:58] Marco Alvarez: Standard pattern is ingest-only for the pilot, instrument tracing, and route 5% traffic with canary fallbacks to the legacy cluster. We'll provide a migration runbook and a test harness. For compliance, ensure the replay pipeline filters or redacts PII on ingest if it leaves region.
[06:16] Paul Mendes: We also need to confirm data deletion semantics for when the pilot completes and we want guaranteed deletion of logs and models trained on transient data. Is there a kill switch?
[06:27] Marco Alvarez: We have deletion APIs and retention policies. For Private you control retention. For Dedicated we can set retention TTLs and perform certified deletion. We'll provide the deletion certificate for compliance.
[06:41] Nina Rao: Great. A couple of nitty gritty items: 1) Can we run hardware-backed HSMs in our tenancy for Dedicated? 2) Will control plane metadata include tenant identifiers that could reveal cross-border mappings?
[06:55] Marco Alvarez: 1) Yes, Dedicated supports HSM-backed KMS in supported regions. 2) Control plane metadata includes tenant id but not payload; we can also mask or hash tenant ids when providing support logs. We can discuss further in the tech deep dive.
[07:12] Ivy Chen: I'm going to capture those as action items.
[07:15] [07:20] Nina Rao: Also, region failures — we may need geo-fallback but not at the cost of violating residency. So we want failover to secondary EU region only, never to US. Is that doable?
[07:30] Marco Alvarez: Yes, routing policies can be set by region. We can route to eu-central as fallback. Automatic failover to other continents would only happen if you opt into cross-region routing.
[07:44] Samir Patel: One more — audit evidence for regulators: incremental snapshots of logs every 24h, and ability to run queries under a privileged role that we control.
[07:56] Marco Alvarez: We can provision read-only audit roles and RBAC via SAML SSO. Also support time-limited presigned exports into your bucket.
[08:07] Paul Mendes: About SSO: we use Okta and require SCIM user provisioning.
[08:12] Ivy Chen: We support Okta SAML and SCIM provisioning for RBAC. We'll include the config guide.
[08:18] Nina Rao: Excellent.
[08:21] [08:30] Speaker 2: quick pricing/term question?
[08:33] Ivy Chen: For pilots we can do a short Dedicated pilot with committed min and overage billing. We'll follow up with a pricing sheet.
[08:40] Nina Rao: High level success criteria for us: 1) no PII leaves EU during pilot, 2) signed BAA for PHI use cases, 3) migration runbook and deletion certificate, 4) evidence for auditors about retention and chain-of-custody.
[08:58] Ivy Chen: Noted. We'll aim to meet those.
[09:02] Marco Alvarez: Tech deep dive will cover network diagrams, KMS flows, and log schemas. We can do 2 hours and invite your infra and security folks.
[09:12] Nina Rao: Prefer late next week.
[09:15] Ivy Chen: I'll propose 2028-09-18 14:00 UTC in the follow-up invite.
[09:20] Samir Patel: Works for me.
[09:22] Paul Mendes: Works.
[09:25] Ivy Chen: Recap and next steps: 1) Ivy to share SOC2, HIPAA attestation summary, log schema, and runbook by 2028-09-13. 2) Marco to run latency/cost estimate and prepare network/KMS diagrams by 2028-09-18. 3) Nina to send list of legal entities that require EU residency by 2028-09-14.
[09:42] Nina Rao: Thanks, that covers it.
[09:45] Ivy Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and the invite.

End of transcript.
